parts.prompt: Explain why Na⁺ is smaller than neutral Na.

steps.text: Nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same main energy level.
Shielding changes relatively little, so effective attraction increases and the electron cloud contracts.
Formation of Na⁺ removes the outer-shell electron, leaving one fewer occupied shell.
There is also less electron–electron repulsion for the same nuclear charge.

steps.text: The electron removed from Al is in 3p, whereas that from Mg is in 3s.
The 3p electron is higher in energy / less strongly held, outweighing the increase in nuclear charge.

Electron–electron repulsion within the pair makes an electron easier to remove from sulfur.

steps.text: They have the same functional-group type / general formula.

Larger electron clouds increase London dispersion forces and thus boiling temperatures.
The non-polar hydrocarbon portion becomes larger relative to the one hydroxy group, making hydration less favourable.

title: Eliminating candidate structures
stem: A liquid has formula C₄H₈O₂. Its proton NMR spectrum has three signals: a 3H singlet, a 2H quartet and a 3H triplet. The quartet is near 4.1 ppm; a strong IR C=O band is present. Data are constructed.

verification.method: Author derivation and automated schema, rendering and numerical checks
verification.notes: Original practice for the first-assessment-2025 syllabus. Marking points are instructional; equivalent chemically valid explanations and appropriate error-carried-forward working are accepted. Separate human examiner moderation has not been performed.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Deduce its structure and assign the three proton sets.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why methyl propanoate does not fit the chemical-shift assignment, despite having the same signal integrals and splitting types.

steps.text: Ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.
CH₃CO gives the singlet; OCH₂ gives the quartet; terminal CH₃ gives the triplet.
Methyl propanoate has OCH₃, so its oxygen-bound proton set is a 3H singlet.
Its 2H quartet is adjacent to carbonyl carbon rather than directly to oxygen, so a 2H quartet near 4.1 ppm favours ethyl ethanoate.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the oxidation state of hydrogen in each and explain the difference.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State why oxidation state is not always the same as the measured charge on an atom in a covalent molecule.

steps.text: NaH: H is −1; HCl: H is +1.
Hydrogen is more electronegative than sodium but less electronegative than chlorine, so electrons are assigned differently in oxidation-state bookkeeping.
Oxidation states use a formal complete-electron-transfer assignment to the more electronegative atom.
Covalent bonding shares electron density, so real partial charges need not be those integer values.

stem: A compound gives a molecular-ion peak at m/z=72 and a prominent fragment at m/z=43. Its IR spectrum shows a strong carbonyl band and no broad O–H. Use C=12, H=1 and O=16.

verification.method: Author derivation and automated schema, rendering and numerical checks

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give a plausible formula for a carbonyl-containing fragment at m/z=43 and one ketone structure consistent with molecular mass 72.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Evaluate the claim that a peak at m/z=43 alone uniquely identifies this ketone.

steps.text: Butan-2-one, CH₃COCH₂CH₃, has molecular formula C₄H₈O and mass 72.
The claim is not justified: different compounds can produce the same fragment, and different fragment formulas can have the same nominal mass.
Combine molecular mass, IR and NMR or other evidence before making a unique assignment.
